mathematics
Mathematics
Maths & technology
Build confidence with equations, shapes and data.
Linear equations
Use inverse operations on both sides to isolate the unknown. Substitute your answer back into the original equation to check it.
Solve 3x + 7 = 22.
Subtract 7 to get 3x = 15. Divide by 3 to get x = 5.
Right-angled trigonometry
Relative to the chosen angle, sine is opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cosine is adjacent ÷ hypotenuse and tangent is opposite ÷ adjacent.
The side opposite θ is 6 cm and the adjacent side is 8 cm. Find θ to one decimal place.
Probability
For equally likely outcomes, divide the number of favourable outcomes by the total number of outcomes.
A bag holds 4 red and 6 blue counters. Find the probability of drawing a red counter at random.
english-language
First Language English
English & humanities
Aa
Read closely and write with purpose.
Inference
An inference is a conclusion supported by clues. Identify the detail and explain how it supports your interpretation.
‘Lina reread the message three times before pressing send.’ What might this suggest about Lina?
She may be nervous about how the message will be received. Rereading it three times suggests she wants to avoid a mistake.
Writer’s effects
Pick a precise word or image. Explain what it suggests and how it shapes the reader’s impression of the scene.
What effect does ‘the wind clawed at the shutters’ create?
‘Clawed’ makes the wind sound like an attacking animal, giving the scene a threatening atmosphere.
Summary writing
Select points that answer the question, combine related ideas and express them concisely in your own words.
Summarise in one sentence: ‘The hall leaked. Several windows were broken. Members had stopped attending because the room was often cold.’
Attendance fell because the poorly maintained hall was cold.
english-literature
Literature in English
English & humanities
Explore how writers shape meaning in poetry, prose and drama.
Imagery
Explain what an image makes you picture and how it changes your reading of a character, setting or theme.
What does ‘a cage of golden bars’ suggest about a wealthy character’s home?
‘Golden’ suggests luxury, while ‘cage’ suggests confinement. The image implies that the character can be privileged and trapped at the same time.
Structure
Track shifts in tone, point of view or pace. Connect a shift to its effect on the reader.
A poem moves from ‘we’ to ‘I’ in its last stanza. Suggest one possible effect.
The shift narrows the focus from a group to one speaker and may highlight isolation.
Drama
Stage directions guide performance. Consider how a pause, gesture or movement changes the audience’s interpretation.
A character says ‘Of course’ after a long pause. How might the pause change the line?
The delay can suggest reluctance or doubt, making an apparent agreement feel uncertain.
biology
Biology
Sciences
Explore living systems from cells to ecosystems.
Osmosis
Water moves through a partially permeable membrane from higher water potential to lower water potential.
Why might potato pieces gain mass in distilled water?
The water outside has higher water potential than the cell contents. Water enters the cells by osmosis, increasing mass.
Photosynthesis
Plants use light energy to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water. Oxygen is released.
Why might brighter light stop increasing the photosynthesis rate?
A different factor, such as carbon dioxide concentration or temperature, may limit the rate.
Inheritance
A dominant allele can affect the phenotype in a heterozygous individual. A Punnett square shows possible offspring genotypes.
For Aa × Aa, what fraction of offspring are expected to have genotype aa?
The possible combinations are AA, Aa, Aa and aa. The expected fraction is 1/4.
chemistry
Chemistry
Sciences
Connect particles, reactions and chemical calculations.
Ionic bonding
An ionic bond is the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions. Ionic compounds form giant lattices.
Why does molten sodium chloride conduct electricity?
Its ions are free to move and carry charge through the liquid.
Balancing equations
Change coefficients to conserve the number of atoms of each element. Leave chemical formulae intact.
Balance Mg + O₂ → MgO.
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Both sides have two magnesium and two oxygen atoms.
Rates of reaction
A higher temperature increases particle kinetic energy and the fraction of collisions with energy at or above the activation energy.
Why does powdered calcium carbonate react faster with acid than the same mass of large chips?
The powder exposes more surface area to the acid, increasing the frequency of collisions.
physics
Physics
Sciences
Explain motion, energy and electricity with worked examples.
Motion
The gradient of a speed–time graph gives the rate of change of speed. The area under it gives distance travelled.
A cyclist travels at a steady 6 m/s for 12 s. Find the distance.
Distance = speed × time = 6 × 12 = 72 m.
Forces
For a constant mass, the resultant force equals mass × acceleration. Use kilograms, metres per second squared and newtons.
A 4 kg object accelerates at 3 m/s². Find the resultant force.
F = ma = 4 × 3 = 12 N in the direction of acceleration.
Circuits
Potential difference equals current × resistance. Components in series carry the same current.
A 6 Ω resistor has a 12 V potential difference across it. Find the current.
computer-science
Computer Science
Maths & technology
Practise algorithms, data representation and logic.
Binary
Each binary place represents a power of two. From the right, the first four place values are 1, 2, 4 and 8.
Convert binary 1011 to decimal.
Trace tables
A trace table records how variables change as an algorithm runs. Track one loop iteration at a time.
Start total at 0. Add 2, then 4, then 6 in a loop. List total after each iteration.
The running totals are 2, 6 and 12.
Boolean logic
An AND operation is true only when both inputs are true. OR is true when at least one input is true. NOT reverses its input.
Evaluate NOT(A AND B) when A is true and B is false.
A AND B is false. NOT false is true.
ict
Information & Communication Technology
Maths & technology
Build practical skills with spreadsheets, databases and digital safety.
Spreadsheet references
A relative cell reference moves when copied. A dollar sign locks the row or column that follows it.
Copy =B2*$E$1 from C2 down to C3. What does the formula become?
=B3*$E$1. The relative row changes and the fixed reference stays E1.
Databases
A primary key uniquely identifies a record. Use field types that match how the data will be stored and queried.
Why is a student ID a better primary key than a surname?
Student IDs can be unique, while several students may share a surname.
Digital security
Phishing uses deceptive messages to make people reveal information or take an unsafe action.
An unexpected email asks you to reset your school password through a link. How can you check it safely?
Go to the school’s known website or ask school IT through a trusted contact method.
geography
Geography
English & humanities
Understand landscapes, populations and human activity.
Population change
Natural increase is the birth rate minus the death rate. Migration also affects total population change.
A country has 18 births and 7 deaths per 1,000 people per year. Find its rate of natural increase.
18 − 7 = 11 per 1,000 people per year, equivalent to 1.1% per year.
River processes
Erosion wears material away. Transportation moves it. Deposition occurs when a river can no longer carry some of its load.
Why does sediment often build up on the inside of a meander?
The current is usually slower on the inside bend, so sediment is more likely to be deposited there.
Map scale
A representative fraction expresses the ratio of map distance to ground distance in the same units.
At 1:50,000, what ground distance does 4 cm represent?
history
History
English & humanities
Build arguments about the past and evaluate historical evidence.
Causes
Distinguish long-term conditions from short-term triggers. Explain how each factor contributed to the outcome.
An alliance system existed for years before a crisis led to war. How could the alliances have contributed?
Alliance commitments could widen a local conflict by drawing in countries that supported the original participants.
Source evaluation
Use a source’s content, origin, audience and purpose to judge how useful it is for a specific question.
What can a wartime recruitment poster tell a historian about recruitment?
It shows the arguments and images used to persuade people. Actual enlistment figures would help assess how recruitment changed.
Comparing explanations
Support each explanation with evidence and use a clear criterion, such as impact or timing, to justify your judgement.
What makes an explanation of a policy’s failure stronger?
It connects specific evidence to the outcome and explains why the factor mattered compared with other causes.
economics
Economics
Business & economics
Think through choices, markets and economic changes.
Opportunity cost
Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative given up when you make a choice.
A student can use a free hour for maths practice, football or reading. They choose maths and would otherwise choose football. What is the opportunity cost?
The benefit they would have gained from playing football.
Demand and supply
Equilibrium is the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. A shift in either curve can change it.
If demand rises and supply is unchanged, what usually happens to equilibrium price and quantity?
Both rise under the usual upward-sloping supply and downward-sloping demand assumptions.
Inflation
Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level. It reduces purchasing power if nominal income stays fixed.
Why might someone on a fixed income buy less when prices rise?
Their income buys fewer goods and services because each unit of money has less purchasing power.
business-studies
Business Studies
Business & economics
Work through business decisions about people, markets and finance.
Break-even
At break-even, total revenue equals total costs. Contribution per unit is selling price minus variable cost per unit.
Fixed costs are $600. Each item sells for $8 and costs $5 in variable costs. Find break-even output.
Contribution is $3 per item. Break-even output is $600 ÷ $3 = 200 items.
Market research
Primary research gathers new data for a specific decision. Secondary research uses data that already exists.
A bakery surveys students about preferred snacks. What type of research is this?
Primary research, because the bakery collects new responses for its own decision.
Cash flow
Net cash flow is inflows minus outflows. A business can run short of cash when customers pay after expenses are due.
A shop opens the month with $300, receives $900 and pays $1,000. Find its closing cash balance.
Net cash flow is −$100. Closing balance is $300 − $100 = $200.
